finding.title: OS Command Injection
finding.trigger: An attacker could input a malicious file name that leads to unintended file access or execution.
finding.assumptions: The application does not sanitize or validate the input file name before using it in file operations.

parsed.refutation_attempt: Checked that the reported sink is Path.Combine, which simply constructs a file path string and does not invoke any OS command or shell. The subsequent operations (File.Exists, GenerateRandomScores, ProcessRoundResults) are file reads/writes or internal processing, not command execution. Therefore no OS command injection is possible. The input is not sanitized, but that would be a path‑traversal risk, not command injection.

finding.title: OS Command Injection
finding.trigger: An attacker could input a malicious directory name or file pattern that leads to unintended file access or execution.
finding.assumptions: The application does not sanitize or validate the input directory name or file pattern before using it in file operations.

parsed.refutation_attempt: Checked the code around lines 88-93, 108-111. The only Directory.GetFiles call is at line 94: Directory.GetFiles(dataDirectory, "round-*.csv"). The variable dataDirectory is set to the literal string "Data" on line 93, and the search pattern "round-*.csv" is also a literal. No user-supplied value from Console.ReadLine() is ever concatenated into the directory path or pattern used in Directory.GetFiles. The user input at line 88 only toggles whether the simulation loop runs and does not influence the directory or pattern. Thus there is no path from an untrusted source to the sink. Also, even in case 2, the user input is used only with Path.Combine("Data", roundFileName) and File.Exists, not with Directory.GetFiles. Therefore the claim of OS command injection is unfounded.

finding.title: OS Command Injection
finding.trigger: An attacker could input a malicious string that leads to unintended output or execution.
finding.assumptions: The application does not sanitize or validate the input string before using it in output operations.

parsed.refutation_attempt: Checked that the reported sink (Console.WriteLine) on lines 119-120 prints only a static string and does not execute any command. Verified that the user input at line 88 is only compared to the literal "y" and, if matched, the code further reads a file path that is validated by File.Exists on line 63 before any processing. No function that invokes an OS command is called with untrusted data. Thus there is no path from untrusted input to a command execution API, refuting the OS Command Injection claim.
